description: Network and command-and-control indicators in assembly source.

rules.name: Socket opened or connected
rules.description: The program creates a network socket or connects it to a remote address. In a sample you did not write, this is the first thing to explain: which address, which port, and what is sent.

rules.name: Hardcoded host or URL
rules.description: An address is embedded in the data section. Even without a single network syscall, a literal host name says where the sample wants to talk.

rules.name: Raw IPv4 literal
rules.description: A dotted-quad address appears in the source. Useful as an indicator, noisy as a verdict: version numbers and masks look the same.

rules.name: HTTP client markers
rules.description: A User-Agent, an HTTP verb or a WinINet/WinHTTP entry point is present: the sample speaks HTTP rather than a custom protocol.

rules.name: DNS resolution
rules.description: The sample resolves a name at runtime (getaddrinfo/gethostbyname or a DNS-oriented API), which often means the address comes from a configuration or a domain-generation scheme.
